refuter_findings.evidence: The entire Statement is the strategy sentence “Use the full-dimension equality to rule out strict containment above a smaller support prime.” It gives no ring, module, hypotheses, or conclusion; the next section instead says “Given: the hypotheses and notation stated above.” Thus no corollary is stated.

The Statement merely says “Apply the localized equality at every support prime and then invoke the global Cohen--Macaulay convention.” It has no domain or asserted localization result, while Facts says “Given: the hypotheses and notation stated above.”

“Use equality of depths from reflection and equality of support dimensions under completion to prove the local-ring and finite-module equivalence” is a proof plan, not an equivalence with hypotheses or conclusion. The purported assumptions are absent.

The Statement is only “Compare the regular-sequence definition with the common Ext length, retaining the infinity case when every relevant Ext group vanishes.” It never specifies the Ext formula, its hypotheses, or its quantifiers.
“The n-generator Koszul complex has no degrees beyond n, and M/IM nonzero excludes the infinity convention” supplies neither a declared setting nor an asserted inequality; it is only a proof cue.

The Statement says only “Translate the equality of first nonzero Ext degrees for equal radicals back into equality of depths.” It does not state ideals, equal-radical hypothesis, module conditions, or conclusion.
“Combine pairs of Depth Lemma inequalities in the standard strict-depth ranges” does not state a short exact sequence, the strict inequalities, or any resulting equality.
The Statement only directs the reader to “Specialize the local-prime bound at the maximal ideal.” It does not declare the local ring/module hypotheses or the inequality.
“Translate depth zero into absence of an M-regular element in I and apply the prime-avoidance lemma” is a strategy, without a stated iff, hypotheses, or quantified associated prime.
“Apply the parameter induction to the full system and retain the terminal nonzero quotient condition” does not identify the ring, module, system, or regularity conclusion.
The Statement refers to unspecified “source-stated dimension-formula hypotheses” and an “iff criterion,” but states neither the hypotheses nor the criterion.
“The split sequence gives one bound; the Ext/Koszul vanishing characterization gives the reverse” is not a depth-additivity formula or a declaration of its flat-local hypotheses.
The Statement is an argument sketch: “A regular system has length equal to support dimension...” It does not state the ambient local data, parameter-system hypothesis, or Cohen--Macaulay conclusion.
“At a polynomial prime compare the one-variable depth and support-dimension increments” does not state which module/ring or any preservation assertion.
“Subtract one from both invariants in the gap lemma to prove the two-way equivalence under its stated hypotheses” supplies neither the hypotheses nor the equivalence.

The Statement says only “The depth upper bound and nonnegative regular-sequence definition force both invariants to equal zero.” The needed local, finite, and nonzero-module hypotheses and conclusion are unstated.
“Compute associated primes of a Cohen--Macaulay hypersurface with zero divisors...” names no hypersurface, associated primes, computation, or conclusion. The item contains no actual example.
The Example says “Use a hypersurface quotient by a nonzerodivisor...” but gives no ring, element, quotient, or verification of either Cohen--Macaulayness or zero divisors.
“Use the same finite regular sequence in a small local quotient and its completion” does not specify a quotient, sequence, completion, or depth calculation.
The Example directs the reader to “Evaluate the regular-sequence and Ext formulations” but supplies no instance or evaluation.
“Work through three short exact sequences chosen so that each Depth Lemma lower bound is attained” supplies none of the three sequences or computations.
“Start with a regular local ring and a nonzero regular element” gives neither ring nor element, so there is no hypersurface or depth computation to verify.
The Example invokes “the coordinate-ring short exact sequence for a union of planes” but identifies no planes, coordinate ring, sequence, or depth values.
“Present a standard module over a singular hypersurface” gives no hypersurface or module and hence no calculation of depth or nonfreeness.
The Example says “Compute a standard non-equidimensional local quotient's support dimension,” but no quotient, associated prime, dimension, or depth is specified.
“In a reducible local quotient choose a parameter in an associated prime” provides no quotient, parameter, associated prime, or depth-gap computation.
The Example directs “Choose a full parameter system in a hypersurface local ring” but supplies neither the ring nor the system to verify.
“Start from a field and iterate the polynomial-extension theorem” is a plan, not a stated polynomial ring, localization, regular sequence, or calculation.
“For a nonzero zero-dimensional Noetherian local ring calculate...” does not supply a ring or any calculation, so it is not an example.

The long Statement begins “Embed N = R/p in M, apply Artin--Rees...” and is solely a proof plan. It does not declare the necessary hypotheses on R, M, p, x, or state the claimed associated-prime conclusion.
“For p in Ass(M), apply the associated-prime depth bound...” is an argument outline, not a lemma statement with ambient hypotheses and quantified equality.
The Statement says “A first parameter avoids all associated primes...” without defining the local ring, module, parameter system, or asserted regularity claim.
“After the first parameter is regular, use the regular-quotient equivalence...” is an induction plan, without a parameter tuple, hypotheses, or induction conclusion.

The Statement is only “Use flat completion to preserve injections and faithful flatness to preserve nonzero terminal quotients.” It does not state the completion, module, sequence, or preservation result.
“Combine preservation with faithful-flat descent...” does not state the local hypotheses, completion, or equality of depths being claimed.
“Each regular element gives a strict support-dimension descent...” is a proof cue; no prime, local module, hypotheses, or numerical inequality is stated.
“Follow the cited Stacks depth lemma: induct on depth...” is a strategy and mentions p, q, x, and M without declaring them or giving a formal lemma conclusion.
“Unpack the infinity convention for IM=M, then use Nakayama...” never states the actual lemma, its ring/module assumptions, or its conclusion.
“Inspect adjacent Ext terms to convert their vanishing range into the lower bound for the left term” does not state a short exact sequence or the lower-bound formula.
The Statement merely instructs “Read the Ext vanishing range for the middle term...” and does not give the exact sequence or claimed inequality.
“Use the remaining adjacent Ext terms to derive the lower bound for the quotient term” omits the exact sequence and the shifted inequality.
Although it contains a prospective formula, the Statement begins “For a prime p prove...” and has no declared ring/module hypotheses; it is an instruction, not a well-formed quantified lemma.
“Use the regular-element Ext shift... to prove depth_I(M/xM)=depth_I(M)-1” leaves R, I, M, x, finiteness, regularity, and convention boundary conditions unstated.
“Use powers witnessing equal radicals and finite quotient filtrations...” contains no ideals, module, Ext degrees, hypotheses, or asserted equality.
“Apply Ext_R(R/I,-) to 0 to M to M to M/xM to 0” is a malformed prose sketch of a sequence and never states the shift theorem or assumptions.
The Statement says “Evaluate Hom_R(R/I,M) at one modulo I...” but gives no ambient assumptions or formal identification/conclusion.
“For a flat local map, base-change a regular sequence...” does not specify the map, rings, modules, sequences, or conclusion.
“Use a finite free Koszul complex and self-duality...” is only a route to a result. The required local, finite, ideal-generator, and formula data are absent.
“Follow the cited Stacks localization lemma. Induct along a maximal prime chain...” gives a strategy but no stated localization theorem or hypotheses.
“Apply the depth-zero associated-prime criterion to the terminal quotient” does not state the ring, ideal, regular sequence, terminal quotient, or obstruction/converse.
“Iterate the Ext shift to a terminal depth-zero quotient...” omits all hypotheses and the claimed common-length theorem.
“Prove coefficientwise that x is regular on M[x]...” does not state the module, prime/localization, or depth equality.
“Identify zero divisors on a nonzero finite module through associated primes...” is a method. It does not state the necessary Noetherian data, ideal hypothesis, or existence conclusion.
“Combine the one-step depth quotient formula with exact parameter dimension drop...” does not declare the local module, parameter, regularity assumptions, or gap equality.
“Package the full quotient-dimension conclusion, minimality in support, and absence of embedded associated primes” does not state a theorem or its hypotheses.
“Package the two-way completion theorem with its Noetherian local, finite-module, and completion-ideal hypotheses” explicitly describes a future statement rather than giving one.
“Record the finite nonzero local-module inequality...” does not record the inequality, ambient data, or zero-module convention it references.
“Package the comparison for finite modules over a Noetherian ring...” is not the claimed theorem and leaves the conditions and conclusion unstated.
“State depth additivity and the Cohen--Macaulay consequence separately...” is an instruction; no flat local map, module data, equality, or consequence is actually stated.
“Assemble the three focused Ext-vanishing inequalities for a short exact sequence...” gives neither the sequence nor any of the three inequalities.
“Specialize the ideal criterion to the maximal ideal of a Noetherian local ring...” does not state the criterion, its module data, or its iff conclusion.
“State the first-nonzero-cohomology and last-nonzero-homology formulations...” is a request for a statement, not the formulations themselves.
“State the finite Noetherian localization theorem in local and global forms...” supplies no theorem, hypotheses, or conclusion.
“State both directions: every parameter system...” is not a formal statement: it does not declare the ring/module data or the exact meaning and hypotheses of either direction.
“Specialize the module result to the ring module...” is a proof plan without a ring, polynomial extension, hypotheses, or conclusion.
“State the source-qualified radical, localization, and one-step quotient results...” declares that results should be stated but does not state any of them.
“Iterate the one-step equivalence along a regular parameter sequence...” is a strategy and omits the ring/module hypotheses and claimed equivalence.

The page says “Examples test the depth convention, Depth Lemma, parameter regularity, completion, and the distinction between Cohen--Macaulayness and being a domain.” Each listed example is instead only an uninstantiated strategy paragraph with “Given: the hypotheses and notation stated above”; none supplies the constructions or computations claimed by this prose.
